PROTECTED_FIELDS.finding: The packet writes into a line of the Article 995 proposed order that its own field map, four lines away, calls court-owned - and the contradiction is in the delivered record, in place. The statute's PLEASE SERVE block prints three identical rows, each a party role followed by a blank: '1. District Attorney ____', '2. Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information ____', '3. Arresting Agency ____'. production-field-map.json refuses rows 1 and 2 as PROTECTED_FIELD with the reason 'Article 979 makes service the clerk's act; the serve list is completed by the clerk', and WRITES row 3 (LA-CCRP-ART-995.serve_arresting_agency, factId case.arresting_law_enforcement_agency). On delivered canonical page 5 that row reads '3. Arresting Agency Tangipahoa Parish Sheriff's Office' while rows 1 and 2 carry only dots. The stated reason for refusing rows 1 and 2 applies with equal force to row 3: if Article 979 makes the serve list the clerk's act, row 3 is the clerk's too. The same family's controlling boundary, reproduced verbatim on delivered guide page 17 and in judicialBoundaryOnTheOrder.statedByTheRecord, is 'LegalEase supplies the caption and the felony charge identifiers and nothing else.' This write is neither caption nor a felony charge identifier, so the delivered order carries a sixth write the delivered record says does not exist. The build script knows: its comment at lines 708-711 says the agency 'IS written, because the platform holds it and because the completeness contract refuses to let an agency name hide inside a court-owned refusal class'. That reasoning reaches no delivered record and no participant - a completeness counter is not a legal basis for writing on a proposed order. What the participant is told is narrower than what happened: participant-instructions.md line 175 says 'Leave the clerk's filed-on stamp, the clerk's certificate of service and the district attorney and Bureau lines of the PLEASE SERVE list blank', naming only rows 1 and 2 and never saying that the packet filled row 3 or why, while lines 130 and 157 of the same file tell the participant 'The participant does not serve anyone.' Actionable repair, for a lane that is not this one: settle the three rows the same way. Either refuse row 3 as court-owned like its two siblings, or write all three and restate the judicial boundary and the guide to match - but not one of each with opposite reasons on the same block of the same order.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.detail: Measured on rendered ink, because the build's own guard cannot fail. Per-page ink bounding boxes at 300 dpi, PGM, threshold 128, annotations ON, all 19 pages of BOTH fixtures: the greatest rightward extent of ink anywhere in the family is 547.44 pt, on pages 10 and 11 of each fixture, against a declared text-box right edge of 552 pt (PAGE_WIDTH 612 - MARGIN 60). Smallest right gutter 64.56 pt. No page reaches 552. Left edge is 60.00 pt on every page but page 13, where it is 59.76 pt - one 300-dpi pixel of left-side bearing at the margin origin, 60 pt from the paper edge. Vertical: minimum baseline gap on any page of either fixture is exactly 13.25 pt against a 10.25 pt Times-Roman glyph box of 11.79 pt (0.9 ascent + 0.25 descent), 0 pairs closer than that, and all 608 text runs on each fixture start at x=60.00 at one size, so no two runs can overlap. THE GUARD THAT CANNOT FAIL, named because the brief asked whether the nine-script shared shape bears on this family: it does, and here is the measurement. The build wraps to WRAP_WIDTH = MAX_WIDTH - WRAP_SAFETY = 484 pt and then asserts `width <= MAX_WIDTH + 0.01` = 492 pt on the same advance sum the wrap just bounded, so the assertion is satisfied by construction for any WRAP_SAFETY >= 0 and can never fire. Measured on the delivered line text with the same font and size the build uses: 608 lines per fixture, widest advance sum 483.96 pt, 0 lines past WRAP_WIDTH, 0 lines past MAX_WIDTH - the assertion had 8.04 pt of slack on the widest line in the packet. What actually protects this family is WRAP_SAFETY, not the assertion: rendered ink runs about 3.5 pt past the advance sum on the widest lines, which is the ~0.6% overshoot FIX142 measured, and 8 pt of wrap safety absorbs it with 4.56 pt to spare. The five other Louisiana families that still overhang are another lane's work and are not touched here; this family's own bytes are inside their box, and the pass rests on this lane's pixels rather than on the build's assertion.
